title: Microsoft Teams: Conditional Access policies for selected meetings
summary: The meeting controls and the differing roadmap and Message Center schedules are supported. Minor corrections should complete the authentication-context path, simplify the Graph calls and distinguish the known Conditional Access licence requirement from unpublished Teams-specific licensing.

claims.claim: The feature permits Conditional Access policies for selected Teams meetings.
claims.quote: Administrators can apply Conditional Access policies to selected meetings, helping ensure participants meet organizational security requirements before joining.

claims.claim: Organisers can select an authentication context for a specific meeting.
claims.quote: $true: Conditional Access Authentication contexts are available for the organizer to select from those published in the Teams Meeting Configuration, defaulting to None in the meeting options dropdown.

claims.claim: MC1532256 identifies multifactor authentication, device compliance and location-based controls as possible additional requirements.
claims.quote: allowing organizers to require additional verification such as multifactor authentication, device compliance, or location-based controls.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends configuring Entra contexts and policies, publishing contexts to Teams and enabling authentication requirements through Teams meeting policies.
claims.quote: administrators should configure required authentication contexts and associated Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra, publish authentication contexts to Microsoft Teams, and enable meeting authentication requirements through Teams meeting policies.

claims.claim: Authentication contexts are managed at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Authentication context.
claims.quote: Manage authentication contexts by going to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Authentication context. Select New authentication context to create an authentication context definition.
claims.fix: Complete controls[0].ui.path and its table rendering as 'Entra ID > Conditional Access > Authentication context > New authentication context > Publish to apps'. The current route stops on the correct management page; the cited page documents the remaining creation and publication steps.

claims.claim: POST /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/authenticationContextClassReferences creates a context with id, displayName, description and isAvailable set to true.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/authenticationContextClassReferences
{"id": "c1", "displayName": "Contoso medium", "description": "Medium protection level defined for Contoso policy", "isAvailable": true}
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api.call and its table rendering to 'POST /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/authenticationContextClassReferences'. Add to the row note: 'The request body supplies id, displayName and description, and sets isAvailable to true to publish the context to apps.'

claims.claim: Publish to apps makes an authentication context available to downstream apps.
claims.quote: Publish to apps checkbox, when selected, advertises the authentication context to apps and makes it available to be assigned. If not selected, the authentication context is unavailable to downstream resources.

claims.claim: The cited Graph context-creation reference documents the beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: The Graph context-creation reference lists Security Administrator and Conditional Access Administrator as supported roles.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts ... This operation supports the following built-in roles ... Security Administrator; Conditional Access Administrator

claims.claim: A policy targets a context through Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > policy > Assignments > Target resources > Select what this policy applies to > Authentication context.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies. ... Admins can select published authentication contexts ... by going to Assignments > Target resources and selecting Authentication context from the Select what this policy applies to menu.

claims.claim: POST /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies can create a policy targeting conditions.applications.includeAuthenticationContextClassReferences with user assignments and grant controls.
claims.quote: includeAuthenticationContextClassReferences | String collection | Authentication context class references include. Supported values are c1 through c25.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and its table rendering to 'POST /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/policies'. Add to its note: 'The request body targets the context through conditions.applications.includeAuthenticationContextClassReferences and supplies user assignments and grant controls.' The cited create-policy reference confirms the POST operation and body structure.

claims.claim: The beta Graph policy API is subject to change and is not supported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Conditional Access policies can target published authentication contexts to define their requirements.
claims.quote: Admins can select published authentication contexts in Conditional Access policies by going to Assignments > Target resources and selecting Authentication context from the Select what this policy applies to menu.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -PublishedEntraAuthenticationContexts <contexts> configures the published contexts, subject to the documented no-effect caveat.
claims.quote: [-PublishedEntraAuthenticationContexts <PSObject>] ... -Identity: The only valid input is Global ... A list of authentication contexts from Microsoft Entra ID that can be applied to Teams meetings for conditional access scenarios.

claims.claim: Each published context entry requires an Id.
claims.quote: Each entry has a required Id (c1-c99), and optional PublishedName (max 50 characters) and PublishedDescription (max 150 characters).

claims.quote: Each entry has a required Id (c1-c99), and optional PublishedName (max 50 characters) and PublishedDescription (max 150 characters).

claims.claim: PublishedDescription is an optional field for each published context.
claims.quote: Each entry has a required Id (c1-c99), and optional PublishedName (max 50 characters) and PublishedDescription (max 150 characters).

claims.quote: If no Conditional Access policy is assigned to an ACRS value the claim might still be issued, because all policy requirements are satisfied.
